title: 電気回路基礎
subtitle: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits
teachers:
FUKASAWA Toru
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: This is a fundamental and important subject in the electrical engineering curriculum. The objective is to acquire a basic knowledge of electrical circuits and develop the ability to analyze and design electrical circuits through physical and mathematical considerations. Students will learn about electric circuits having resistance (R) that are connected to DC power sources. Particular emphasis will be placed on how to formulate and solve the network equations based on Ohm’s law and Kirchhoff’s law.
advice:
Below is an outline of the topics to be covered:

DC circuits: electric circuits and Ohm’s law, Kirchhoff’s law, superposition principle, Thevenin’s Theorem, Δ-Y conversion, electric power, electric power quantity Calculation

This subject is not only important as preparation for subsequent courses (Electrical Circuit I, Electrical Circuit II, and Electrical Circuit III), but also each specialized topic should be studied keeping in mind that it is a special basic course requirement.
Since the progress is adjusted while checking the level of student understanding indicated by quiz results, etc., changes may occur in the class schedule and the course content.
books: Basic electric circuit (2nd edition) New Edition, Morikita Publishing Co., Ltd.
requiredKnowledge: It is important that you solve as many problems as possible in order to understand and practice the theory presented. In addition, continuous effort is required on a daily basis. Therefore, we encourage you to 1) examine various reference books, 2) ask the lecturer questions, and 3) take advantage of the Mathematical and Science Education Research Center so that you can clarify what you don’t understand.

activityGoals.body: Participants can explain Ohm’s and Kirchhoff’s law in DC circuits.
Participants can formulate and solve equations for DC networks.
Participants can calculate the maximum power condition in DC circuits.
Participants can calculate DC circuits using the superposition principle and Thevenin's theorem.

achievementLevels.ideal: Participants can sufficiently explain the physical and mathematical implications of Ohm’s and Kirchhoff’s laws. Using their knowledge, they can correctly calculate voltages, currents, and energy in DC circuits. They can also fully explain the equilibrium conditions of a bridge circuit. They can sufficiently explain the superposition principle and Thevenin’s theorem and correctly apply them to DC circuits.
achievementLevels.standard: Participants can explain the basic physical and mathematical implications of Ohm’s and Kirchhoff’s laws. Using their knowledge, they can calculate voltages, currents and energy in the DC circuits. They can also explain the equilibrium conditions of a bridge circuit. They can explain the superposition principle and Thevenin’s theorem and apply them to DC circuits.
